title: Artificial Intelligence Interventions in Mathematics Education: A Systematic Literature Review
extended_summary:
This paper presents a systematic literature review of empirical studies published from 2020 to 2024 on artificial intelligence interventions in mathematics education. The review asks two main questions: what kinds of AI-based interventions are being used in mathematics classrooms, and what impact these interventions have on student outcomes such as academic performance, engagement, and personalization. The authors position the review as addressing a gap in prior work by focusing specifically on classroom-based mathematics applications rather than broader STEM or theoretical AI-in-education discussions.

The interventions reviewed include intelligent tutoring systems (ITS), adaptive learning platforms, AI-powered educational applications such as Photomath and ChatGPT, and a smaller number of other tools such as AI-supported virtual reality and AI engines for task personalization. Across the 14 included empirical studies, the review synthesizes findings on outcomes including mathematics achievement, problem-solving, engagement, and some teaching-related outcomes. The review follows PRISMA procedures, searched multiple databases, and included both quantitative and qualitative studies.

The reviewed studies span elementary through postsecondary education and were conducted across multiple countries, including the United States, Slovakia, Philippines, Israel, Spain, Nigeria, Argentina, Taiwan, South Korea, Sweden, and Jordan. Most studies focused on students, though some examined teachers or preservice teachers. The instructional context emphasized classroom-integrated AI tools in mathematics domains such as fractions, arithmetic, algebra, and pre-calculus, with intervention durations ranging from very short sessions to a full school year.

The review concludes that AI tools in mathematics education are generally promising, especially ITS and adaptive platforms used over sustained periods and aligned with instructional goals. Larger effects were associated with longer-duration interventions and with tools providing personalized instruction and real-time feedback; for example, Photomath and some adaptive systems showed moderate to large effects. At the same time, the authors stress that impact depends heavily on context, duration, and teacher involvement, and that shorter interventions or poorly integrated tools tend to show smaller or more limited gains. They also highlight ethical issues such as privacy, fairness, transparency, and the continuing importance of teachers in mediating AI use.

identified_tools.name: ITS
identified_tools.description: Intelligent tutoring systems are AI-based instructional systems that provide step-by-step guidance, adaptive support, hints, and feedback during learner problem solving.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies published 2020-2024. ITS interventions appeared in 6 of the 14 empirical studies reviewed across elementary through post-secondary settings.

findings.finding_summary: ITS were the most frequently studied intervention type in the review and were generally associated with improved mathematics learning outcomes. The review highlights positive examples including WMAL for fractions (d = 0.39), HINTS for arithmetic problem solving (d = 0.58), and a dialogue-based fractions ITS (d = 0.59), with stronger effects reported for more sustained use.
findings.measure: mathematics performance, fraction understanding, arithmetic problem-solving proficiency, post-test performance

findings.finding_summary: ITS effectiveness was context-dependent: shorter interventions and implementations without substantial teacher involvement tended to yield smaller or more limited gains. The review also notes null or limited findings in some ITS-related studies, including no statistically significant effect for ALEKS on end-of-course algebra exam scores.
findings.measure: end-of-course algebra exam scores; duration- and context-sensitive mathematics outcomes

identified_tools.name: Adaptive learning systems
identified_tools.description: Adaptive learning systems are AI-based educational platforms that personalize content, pacing, sequencing, or task selection based on learner performance or interaction data.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies from 2020-2024. This category covers adaptive platforms such as ALEKS and Learn with ME used across elementary through high school and teacher-education contexts.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports positive mathematics outcomes in several studies of adaptive learning platforms, including Learn with ME (d = 0.49).
findings.measure: math performance and learning gains on adaptive platform interventions

findings.finding_summary: Adaptive platforms were also associated with positive engagement indicators in some studies; for example, 82.3% of students using Learn with ME reported the software was enjoyable and engaging.
findings.measure: student enjoyment and engagement with adaptive platform use

findings.finding_summary: Effects were not uniform and depended on implementation conditions. The review notes smaller effects for shorter interventions or those lacking substantial teacher involvement, and includes ALEKS as an example where one study found no statistically significant effect on end-of-course algebra exam scores.
findings.measure: mathematics achievement under varying implementation conditions, including algebra exam scores

identified_tools.name: AI-powered educational apps
identified_tools.description: AI-powered educational apps are learner-facing applications that use AI to support mathematics problem solving, guidance, or interactive instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies published 2020-2024. This heterogeneous category includes app-based tools such as Photomath used in high school to undergraduate settings.

findings.finding_summary: The review highlights strong positive findings for some AI-powered mathematics apps, especially Photomath, which was reported to improve pre-calculus performance by 59.4% with a large effect size (d = 1.37).
findings.measure: pre-calculus performance and problem-solving outcomes

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: ChatGPT is a large language model-based conversational AI system that generates natural language responses to user prompts and can provide explanations, dialogue, and problem-solving support.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis across two mathematics education studies in secondary and undergraduate/university settings where ChatGPT was integrated into instruction or explored as a support tool for mathematics teaching and learning.

findings.finding_summary: Across the reviewed ChatGPT studies, the tool was reported as helpful for basic mathematical problem solving and for supporting comprehension, but less effective for complex mathematics such as geometry and for correcting misconceptions. The review presents ChatGPT as promising but limited without human intervention.
findings.measure: mathematical problem solving, comprehension of concepts, misconception correction

findings.finding_summary: The review reports increased student engagement when ChatGPT was integrated into mathematics instruction, though positive engagement outcomes appeared to depend on educator readiness and support.
findings.measure: student engagement with mathematics instruction using ChatGPT

findings.finding_summary: Implementation findings for ChatGPT emphasized professional development needs. In one teacher-focused study summarized by the review, only 17% of surveyed teachers were aware of ChatGPT, suggesting barriers to broader adoption despite instructional promise.
findings.measure: teacher awareness and readiness for ChatGPT integration

identified_tools.name: AI-enhanced virtual reality
identified_tools.description: AI-enhanced virtual reality systems combine immersive virtual environments with AI-driven functions such as recognition, interaction, or automated feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis based on one study of university students in a teacher education program using smart VR with AI-driven speech recognition and feedback to train mathematical questioning strategies over four weeks.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that AI-enhanced VR improved teacher candidates' mathematical questioning strategies in the included study. One participant improved from a baseline median of 28.6% to 100% post-intervention, and both participants reached 100% mastery of targeted questioning strategies, though the very small sample limits generalizability.
findings.measure: mastery of targeted mathematical questioning strategies

identified_tools.name: AI engines for arithmetic practice
identified_tools.description: AI engines for arithmetic practice are systems that automatically generate, recommend, or adapt mathematics practice tasks based on learner needs or performance.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis based on one ethnographic primary-school study in Sweden (N=250) using an AI engine to personalize mathematics practice tasks over two six-week sessions.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that the AI engine showed potential for personalizing student practice and supporting individual learning in primary mathematics, but frequent teacher intervention was needed to adjust automatically generated tasks.
findings.measure: personalized mathematics practice support and classroom usability

findings.finding_summary: Implementation findings indicated that fully automated task generation was insufficient on its own. The review notes algorithmic biases and frequent teacher adjustment of tasks, underscoring limits of automation and the need to integrate such systems with traditional teaching practices.
findings.measure: teacher mediation needs and suitability of automated task generation in classroom implementation

identified_tools.name: Photomath
identified_tools.description: An AI-powered mathematics tutoring app that allows students to solve math problems, including by taking pictures of equations, and receive solution support.
identified_tools.use_case: The review identifies Photomath as an AI-powered educational app studied by Capinding (2023) with high school students in pre-calculus. It is discussed as a tool that enhanced students’ self-reliance, interest, and performance, and as one of the strongest-performing interventions in the review.

findings.finding_summary: Photomath significantly improved students’ pre-calculus performance in the reviewed study.
findings.measure: Cohen's d; percent improvement from pre-test to post-test

findings.finding_summary: The intervention produced a 59.4% improvement in performance from pre-test to post-test over six weeks.
findings.measure: Performance improvement

identified_tools.name: ALEKS
identified_tools.description: Adaptive online learning platform for mathematics that assesses student knowledge and delivers individualized practice and instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: The review discusses ALEKS in Phillips et al. (2020) as a supplement to high school algebra instruction and in Shin (2022) as one of the ITS tools prospective teachers integrated into lesson plans to address individual learning gaps through real-time assessment. The review presents mixed findings: no significant algebra exam effect in one classroom implementation study, but moderate gains in teacher TPACK when ITS tools including ALEKS were meaningfully integrated.

findings.finding_summary: In the reviewed randomized controlled trial, ALEKS showed no statistically significant effect on end-of-course algebra exam scores compared with the comparison condition.
findings.measure: End-of-course algebra exam scores

findings.finding_summary: In Shin (2022), integration of ITS tools including ALEKS was associated with moderate improvement in prospective teachers’ technological pedagogical content knowledge when the systems were positioned as instructional partners.
findings.measure: TPACK scores

identified_tools.name: Learn with ME
identified_tools.description: Educational software for mathematics that uses adaptive learning paths and error pattern identification to personalize instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: The review identifies Learn with ME in Annuš and Kmet’ (2024) as an adaptive learning platform for elementary students. It is described as personalizing math education and improving performance and engagement over a nine-month intervention.

findings.finding_summary: Students using Learn with ME showed significant improvements in mathematics performance compared with the control group.
findings.measure: Cohen's d

findings.finding_summary: The review reports significant performance gains among elementary students using the adaptive platform over nine months.
findings.measure: Mathematics performance

findings.finding_summary: Most students reported that Learn with ME was enjoyable and engaging.
findings.measure: Student report of enjoyment/engagement

identified_tools.name: Woot Math Adaptive Learning
identified_tools.description: An adaptive digital tutor for fractions designed to personalize mathematics learning and support conceptual understanding.
identified_tools.use_case: The review discusses Woot Math Adaptive Learning (WMAL) in Bush (2021) and Cohen et al. (2021). It was used with 4th and 5th grade students to improve fraction understanding and to compare machine personalization with teacher personalization in a mathematics applet context.

findings.finding_summary: Students using Woot Math Adaptive Learning showed significant improvement in fraction achievement compared with traditional instruction.
findings.measure: Cohen's d; assessment score improvement; percentile gain
findings.effect_size: d = 0.39; 5.9% assessment score improvement; 10.9 percentile point gain

findings.finding_summary: In the comparison of human versus machine personalization, teacher-assigned applets were more challenging than machine-assigned ones, and in 4th grade there was no significant performance difference between teacher-assigned and machine-assigned groups.
findings.measure: Cohen's d; performance comparison

identified_tools.name: HINTS
identified_tools.description: The Hypergraph Intelligent Tutoring System, an intelligent tutoring system that enforces the use of multiple strategies for arithmetic word problems.
identified_tools.use_case: The review reports HINTS in Del Olmo-Muñoz et al. (2022) as an ITS used with 5th and 6th grade students for intra-task flexibility-based training in arithmetic problem solving. It is presented as a successful ITS intervention with moderate positive effects.

findings.finding_summary: Use of HINTS significantly improved students’ arithmetic problem-solving proficiency.
findings.measure: Cohen's d; percent improvement in problem-solving performance

identified_tools.name: MathSpring
identified_tools.description: An adaptive intelligent tutoring system for K-12 mathematics designed to support mastery and self-regulated learning.
identified_tools.use_case: The review discusses MathSpring in Kooken et al. (2021) as an adaptive ITS used with middle school students in the United States and Argentina. It was examined in relation to the Cyclical Self-Regulated Learning Simulation Model and mathematics mastery.

findings.finding_summary: Students from Argentina showed higher mastery scores post-test than students from the United States in the MathSpring study, reflecting a small-to-medium positive effect.
findings.measure: Mastery scores; Cohen's d

findings.finding_summary: Within MathSpring, higher levels of self-regulation, grit, and positive emotions were significantly associated with increased mathematics mastery.
findings.measure: Association with mastery within ITS

identified_tools.name: ASSISTments
identified_tools.description: Online mathematics practice and homework platform that provides immediate feedback, scaffolded problem support, and teacher reports on student performance and progress.
identified_tools.use_case: The review includes ASSISTments in Park (2023) as an ITS used to identify unproductive learning patterns such as wheel-spinning among middle and high school students. It is described as offering targeted feedback and helping many students master key skills after initial practice, while also revealing subgroups who needed more support.

findings.finding_summary: Most students benefited from ASSISTments, with 65-71% mastering key skills after initial ITS practice, but some subgroups showed wheel-spinning and needed additional support.
findings.measure: Skill mastery after initial practice

identified_tools.name: MATHia
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring system for mathematics that provides individualized, step-by-step guidance and support.
identified_tools.use_case: The review mentions MATHia in Shin (2022) as one of the ITS tools prospective secondary mathematics teachers integrated into lesson plans. It is discussed as part of a set of systems used to support individualized instruction and meaningful technology integration.

findings.finding_summary: Use of ITS tools including MATHia was associated with moderate improvement in prospective teachers’ TPACK when the systems were positioned as partners rather than servants.
findings.measure: TPACK scores

identified_tools.name: Khan Academy
identified_tools.description: Mastery-based online learning platform that provides instructional content, practice, progress tracking, and personalized pacing across subjects, including mathematics.
identified_tools.use_case: The review mentions Khan Academy in Shin (2022) as one of the ITS tools prospective secondary mathematics teachers integrated into lesson plans. It is treated as a mathematics education tool used to provide individualized, step-by-step support in planning instruction.

findings.finding_summary: ITS tools including Khan Academy were linked to moderate gains in prospective teachers’ technological pedagogical content knowledge when used as instructional partners.
findings.measure: TPACK scores

identified_tools.name: AI Engine
identified_tools.description: An adaptive intelligent tutoring or task-generation engine designed to automate parts of teaching and personalize student practice in mathematics.
identified_tools.use_case: The review discusses AI Engine in Sperling et al. (2022) as an adaptive system used in Swedish primary mathematics education to generate personalized tasks. It is described as having personalization potential but requiring frequent teacher intervention to adjust automatically generated tasks.

findings.finding_summary: The AI Engine demonstrated potential for personalizing student practice and supporting individual learning, but frequent teacher intervention was needed to adjust its automatically generated tasks.
findings.measure: Qualitative classroom observations

identified_tools.name: Smart VR application
identified_tools.description: A smart virtual reality application with AI-driven speech recognition and feedback capabilities used for instructional training.
identified_tools.use_case: The review includes a smart VR application in King et al. (2024) used with university students in a teacher education program to deliver behavioral skills training in mathematical questioning strategies. It is discussed as improving pedagogical performance, though evidence is limited by a very small sample.

findings.finding_summary: The smart VR application improved participants’ mastery of targeted mathematical questioning strategies, with one participant improving from a baseline median of 28.6% to 100% and both reaching 100% mastery post-intervention.
findings.measure: Performance percentage; mastery of targeted strategies

quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review using PRISMA methods and multiple databases, which strengthens rigor, but it is not a formal meta-analysis and includes heterogeneous study designs and contexts that limit causal certainty and generalizability.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports multiple included studies with effect sizes above 0.20, including moderate to large positive effects for several AI mathematics interventions, indicating meaningful positive impact overall despite variation across studies.
